scheme: Area Licence Scheme then Electronic Road Pricing
charge_note: SGD 0.50-6 per gantry passage, varying by road, time and vehicle class, revised quarterly against measured speeds.
traffic_metric: Expressway volume during ERP hours. Average speeds rose from 35 to 55 km/h.
revenue_note: Treated as general revenue, not hypothecated.
equity_regime: No income-based discounts; the rate varies by congestion, not by driver.
source: Singapore LTA; Menon, Electronic Road Pricing experience and lessons
lesson: Rates revised quarterly against measured speeds, rather than fixed in statute, are what keeps a charge working for fifty years.

charge_note: GBP 5 daily at launch, GBP 15 today, flat regardless of distance or number of entries.
traffic_metric: Traffic within the charging zone, first year. Congestion during charging hours fell about 30%.
revenue_note: Hypothecated to transport for the first ten years.
equity_regime: 90% residents' discount; low-income and disabled residents protected to 2030; motorbikes, mopeds and 9+ seat vehicles exempt.
source: Transport for London, first-year results; SFCTA case studies
lesson: Traffic stayed down permanently but DELAY reverted to pre-charge levels within five years, as road space was reallocated and background demand grew. A charge buys a traffic reduction more reliably than it buys a lasting delay reduction.

charge_note: 11-45 SEK per passage by time of day, daily maximum 135 SEK as of 2023. Pilot ran January to July 2006.
traffic_metric: Cordon crossings during charged hours. The reduction INCREASED over the following decade rather than decaying.
revenue_note: Hypothecated to road and transit investment.
equity_regime: No income-based discounts of any kind.
source: Swedish Transport Administration; Borjesson et al., The Swedish congestion charges: ten years on; Eliasson ITF DP 2016-13
lesson: A scheme with NO income discounts is still not regressive, because wealthy inner-city residents pay the most. Geography did the distributional work that a means test would otherwise have to.

charge_note: 9-22 SEK per passage by time of day, on the same model as Stockholm.
traffic_metric: Total volume across the charged area during charged hours, first year. Inner-city streets about -9%.
revenue_note: Net social surplus of about EUR 20M/year in published cost-benefit analysis.
equity_regime: No income-based discounts; a company-car exemption that worsens the Suits index.
source: Borjesson & Kristoffersson, The Gothenburg congestion charges: cost-benefit analysis and distribution effects
lesson: The company-car exemption moves the Suits index from -0.06 to -0.13. An exemption granted for administrative convenience can double a scheme's regressivity.

charge_note: EUR 5 daily for the Area C cordon since 2012. The 2008 Ecopass charged by emissions class instead.
traffic_metric: Daily vehicle entries to the cordon, 2012 against 2011 (131,898 falling to 90,849). A separate source reports -34%.
source: Comune di Milano open data; C40 Cities case study
lesson: An emissions-based charge was replaced by a congestion-based one, because charging the wrong externality does not fix the right one.

charge_note: USD 9 peak for passenger cars entering Manhattan south of 60th St, charged once per day.
traffic_metric: Vehicles entering the Congestion Relief Zone, first year: 27 million fewer, about 70,000 fewer per day.
revenue_note: USD 550M net in year one, about USD 50M above projection.
equity_regime: Seven categories: 50% low-income discount after the first 10 trips in a month (AGI at or under USD 50k, or SNAP), a tax credit for zone residents under USD 60k, disability, organisational disability, emergency, bus and government exemptions.
source: MTA; New York Governor's office first-anniversary release; Cornell PM2.5 study
lesson: The only North American scheme and the closest comparator this study has. PM2.5 down 22%, crashes down 7%, fatalities in the zone down 40%.

source: Edinburgh referendum, February 2005; Scottish Cabinet papers
lesson: Rejected 74.4% to 25.6%. The driver was TRUST, not economics: only one in four believed the revenue would actually go to transport. Car ownership predicted the vote better than income did.

charge_note: Peak-only, two cordons, attached to a GBP 3bn transport package.
lesson: A GBP 3bn transport package attached to the charge was not enough to carry it. Paying people in advance does not buy consent if they do not believe the charge will work.

charge_note: USD 8 cordon proposed under the federal Urban Partnership programme.
lesson: Failed in the state legislature, not at the ballot box, and forfeited USD 354M of federal funding. Seventeen years passed before the 2025 scheme. Losing an authorisation fight is not a delay, it is a generation.
